english: It rained. Then the gods arrived together, and the Father was sitting above. Then Mother Earth stood up and called on Sky: "Father, hear me! And you, dear gods, listen to me. Heavy to me are the men, the cattle and the sheep. My heart is heavy, and I have grown tired. Who shall lift these men from me?" Then he spoke to her: "Mother, I have heard your word. Old men will die, and they will lie down in the earth. Then you will not be heavy. May the gods give you rest." Then they heard his word and became joyful. Then she sat down in peace. Death comes to old men, and she protects them. In the spring men give her a gift.

english: The serpent was crawling in the marsh and spoke: "No one has overpowered me. I have enclosed the waters, and I am great. My teeth are many." The rivers were not flowing, and the men were thirsty. The tears of the men fell. Perkwunos was listening well. He heard its word, and he stood up, and he seized bronze, and he came. Then Perkwunos said: "Might is mine. I shall slay you." Then the serpent seized Perkwunos. Perkwunos thundered, and he slew the serpent with bronze. Then the waters became free. They set great fame on him, and men listen to his famous name. He is the slayer of the serpent, and they make a hymn for him. Great is his stature.

english: A swift god stole the cattle of Sky in the night and drove them to the field. Then he drove them to the river, and the cattle were swimming. Then he hid them in the marsh. An old man was sitting at the door. The old man was listening well. He saw the god and recognized him. At dawn Sky looked at his own cattle and did not see them. Then he called the old man: "Who has taken my cattle?" Then the old man said: "The god took them. I saw him." Then the Father was saying: "Swift god, you stole my cattle. Lead them back!" english: A wife was walking on the path and crying out. Her husband had died, and her tears fell. It dawned, and Dawn came forth to her. The wife looked at her and called on her: "Dawn, daughter of Sky, hear me! My husband has died. What shall I do?" Then Dawn said: "Wife, do not cry out! I have heard you. Death comes to men, but fame does not die. I shall give you a son. He will be of good fame, and his might will be great." Then the wife asked: "What shall I give you?" Then Dawn said: "Give me a hymn." Then the wife made a hymn for Dawn and gave her a gift. Then Dawn vanished. In the year a son came to her. His name was famous.

english: It dawned. Dawn, the daughter of Sky, stood up and was saying to the people. "Wake up, people! I am coming, and I am red, and I bring you light. Shepherd, stand up and lead the sheep to it! Man, wake up and yoke the cattle with the yoke! Wife, rise, milk the cattle, heat the water and cook the grain! Sons and daughters, do not lie down! Old man, sit at the door and look at the path. If you do not rise, the Sun will see you lying down. Who has risen? To him I shall give good fame. Give me a hymn, and I shall give you good things." Then the people woke up, and the Sun shone out. The shepherd led the sheep, the man yoked the cattle, and the wife milked them.

english: Earth called on Sky: "Sky, my husband, hear me! I am thirsty, and the field has dried up. The rivers do not flow. My sheep are thirsty, and my cattle lie down. My heart is heavy. Drive the clouds! Give thunder! Let it rain! If it rains, the grain will grow, and the sheep will drink. I shall give you grain and a hymn." Then he said: "My wife, I have heard your word. Last year you gave me no gift." Then she answered: "Last year it did not rain. If it rains, I shall give you a gift." Then he said: "I shall drive the clouds, and the thunder will roar." Then it rained, and the rivers became full. The grain grew in it, and they drank. She made a hymn for him.
